specification.title: Managed transaction: catch a unique violation, then return normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary callback or context-manager API.
Write the marker `tx` and make sure the write was sent.
Insert the duplicate value 'taken' into uniq. Catch the unique violation at the application layer. Send nothing else.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. Send no query.
Allow the callback or context manager to finish normally, so the framework uses its ordinary completion path.
Checkpoint `after-api`: report the same backend PID as soon as that API has returned, before any reuse.
On the same pool or connection, run one new transaction that writes the marker `reuse` and commits. Checkpoint `reuse-after-write` if that transaction starts.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the case function has returned.

invariants.statement: The run recorded the application-visible outcome and an independent database outcome that agree with each other. This invariant does not judge whether the application-visible outcome was the correct commit report. That judgment is in the research summary.

execution.description: DriverManagerDataSource. A connection is opened for the transaction and closed when Spring releases it. No pool. The outer TransactionTemplate uses the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. A nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. TX-03 is not run in this mode (not-applicable-by-design). On this server, DataSourceUtils.releaseConnection closed a connection whose autocommit was false, and that backend was gone from pg_stat_activity. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCleanupAfterCompletion unbinds the holder and then calls releaseConnection, which closes the connection because it is no longer bound. The next TransactionTemplate ran on a different backend. This DataSource cannot hand a transactionally active connection to later work.
execution.form: TransactionTemplate.execute. The callback catches DataAccessException and returns. Writes use JdbcTemplate.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application. No statement is withheld or rewritten.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction API finishes.
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction unless the application has recovered through a savepoint. This variant does not create a savepoint.
fault.expected_client: The application catches 23505. The framework then finishes the transaction through its ordinary API.

knowledge: The application caught the unique violation. Whether PostgreSQL's later reply is visible depends on the driver and the framework.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute returned normally, so the template committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism."

violation.message: PreparedStatementCallback; SQL [insert into uniq (code) values (?)]; ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" Detail: Key (code)=(taken) already exists.

evaluation.mechanism_detail: at before-end the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)"; at after-api the session had closed
evaluation.reason: PR-01.1 held: the API reported committed; at before-end the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)"; at after-api the session had closed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
a unique_violation (23505) was observed on the failing statement
the marker visibility agrees with pg_xact_status() for the captured transaction
